Product Description The tantalizing tale of Catherine returns with all new dilemmas and puzzles in Catherine: Full Body. As the lines blur between nightmare and reality, freedom and commitment, what will become of Vincent Brooks? Your choices and the moral consequences that follow will determine his fate. Catherine: Full Body features a number of brand-new cutscenes, animated cinematics, and entirely new branching story paths. • A Full-Bodied Remaster: The captivating tale of 2011’s award-winning Catherine returns in Catherine: Full Body - bigger and better than before. Improved visuals and gameplay, brand-new music, enhanced multiplayer options, and much more await in this enticing new package. • From a Love Triangle to a Love Square: Explore brand-new branching story paths centering around the arrival of the mysterious amnesiac, Rin. Dozens of new cutscenes and animated cinematics have been added to delve even deeper into Vincent’s complicated present life, as well as his past. • Puzzling Puzzles – If You Desire: Looking for a challenge? Catherine: Full Body contains over 500 puzzles, over twice that of the original game! ‘Arrange Mode’ adds complex linked blocks to once-familiar levels, requiring new techniques and strategies to conquer them. With the addition of this new mode, new difficulties, and a ton of new stages added to Stray Sheep’s ‘Rapunzel’ mini-game, Catherine: Full Body contains over 500 puzzles, over twice that of the original game! • It’s Not Cheating: Just looking to enjoy the story? ‘Safety Mode’ gives players the option to skip any puzzle, letting you sit back and enjoy Vincent’s tragic tale. List of ChangesThis is basically the same game released in 2011 with some added changes; namely a new love interest Rin or Catherine with a Q? Qatherine. So now the love triangle is now a love square. Similar concept to Persona 3 and 4 with Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden. New added story lines and some game play tweaks. Before I go through list of changes, let's go through the basic premise of the game: Very story heavy, slice of life game. Gameplay revolve around playing a Q-bert style puzzle platformer game where you push, pull and maneuver blocks to dodge traps and climb a crumbling tower to reach the top. You enter these puzzle segments when our main protagonist Vincent (no relation) gets nightmares at night about his fiance Katherine since he's not willing to commit to marrying her (along with having possible feelings with Catherine and Rin), and has to climb a tower before whatever chasing him catches him and kills him. Rumor around the bar says that if you die in your dreams you die in real life like the 'Nightmare on Elm street' movie (unless you play on the new safety mode). When you reach the top, you are put into a confession booth where you answer questions about your relationship moving this 'order and freedom' (good and evil, morality type meter) that helps determine what 1 of 13 possible endings you'll eventually get. Climbing the tower is a metaphor for what Vincent is experiencing in real life. During the day you partake in interacting with NPCs at the Stray Sheep bar, taking to Kathrine, Catherine and/or Rin, and answering text on your phone. That may or may not influence the morality meter. There's this supernatural element in the game also that revolves around Catherine, and a mystery of why everyone getting nightmares and dying from them --- Now onto the list of changes I've noticed: 1. Qatherine Or Rin for short. New female(?) love interest. Like Katherine (with a K) lives in the real world. Bumps into your main protagonist Vincent, who finds out she has amnesia and homeless(?). You help her get a job at the bar/pizza joint and is conveniently your new next door neighbor. Rin is integrated into the story well. She's put in very naturally like she was part of deleted scenes or extended cut of the original game and doesn't feel tacked on. Unlike Catherine, you needs to go out of their way to begin a relationship with Rin. On day 6, choosing certain options will begin Rin's branch of the story. If you do not want to go through it for some reason (if you don't swing that way), then the original story plays out but with options of 2 more possible endings (total) for Catherine and Katherine 2. New songs. Added soundtrack. Juke box in bar now includes new Persona songs released after 2011. 3. Remix modes Those who are familiar with/memorize the puzzles; there are now remixed puzzles dubbed "Arrange mode" to make the game feel new. 4. 180 degree rotation When you go behind a block, the camera auto rotates 180 degrees 5. Edge highlighter When you go into a block there's a blue highlights that tells you where you can traverse. 6. New photo/text New photo and text conversations during cell phone segments 7. New cutscenes/ ending 20 new animated cutscene Ones for Katherine, Catherine flush out the characters more. Katherine now feels less bossy and more empathetic 5 new endings: Rin True Ending Rin Good Ending Rin Bad Ending Catherine Alternate Ending Katherine Alternate Ending 8. New patrons to the bar Two new characters who enter the Stray Sheep bar; Roderick and Abul. Shows up during Vincent's nightmares 9. New easier, safety mode. For those who just want to enjoy the story. No game overs, no time limit, able to skip puzzles, option to let cpu autoplay 10. Time freeze mechanic Rin's piano has the power to freeze collapsing stage, activated automatically when Vincent is in an emergency in certain stages. A green light appears as the piano's melody is heard. 11. 500 new stages Some part of remixed stages as mentioned before. Also new stages in Rapunzel mini-game which has been renamed "Super Rapunzel". Mini game also has Standard and Arrange mode 12. Online battle mode Able to play ranked or random matches Overall fun Q-bert style puzzle platformer with a choose your own adventure game. Know that the game is very story heavy and may not interest some.MoreHideThank you for your feedbackCloseSorry, there was an errorCloseSorry we couldn't load the reviewTry again Top reviews from the United States There was a problem filtering reviews. Nicholas5.0 out of 5 stars This game must've been written by psychologists Reviewed in the United States on August 3, 2020Verified Purchase It directly deals with a societal dilemma that we are currently witnessing, most know it as "peter pan syndrome" in that men simply either refuse to grow up or stumble over the choice to grow up. Growing up doesn't just happen, it's literally a choice that one makes.This game is set in a bar, in which the main character (32m) along with his friends are alcoholics and in longterm relationships but haven't made long-term commitments. The girlfriends want to move on to the next level (marriage, family) but for some reason there are major psychological walls that the men have to overcome.This is when the nightmares start, in that the men have to figure a way to climb over those walls to get to the next level. They start encouraging each other along the way and dealing with personal issues and mental roadblocks that you overhear other men struggling with.At the end of each round is a question that the player must answer. For example, after overcoming the first wall, the first question posed to the gamer is, "Do you believe that marriage is the beginning or end of life?" The answers are either "the beginning" or "the end." After the question is answered, it shows you a pie chart as to how ALL other gamers (both men and women) answered that question. I was shocked at the overall responses of some of the questions.Anyways, it was a great game. SUPER challenging and literally makes you reflect on your own mental roadblocks that you are either dealing with or refusing to deal with. Read more 10 people found this helpful Helpful Report Mister Blue Sky4.0 out of 5 stars A Mind-Bending Thrill Ride Reviewed in the United States on April 30, 2023Verified Purchase As a longtime fan of puzzle games and thrilling narratives, I was immediately drawn to Catherine: Full Body on PS4. And let me tell you, this game does not disappoint!First off, the visuals are stunning. The art style is unique and eye-catching, and the characters are well-designed and memorable. The voice acting is top-notch as well, with each character bringing their own personality and flair to the game.But what really sets Catherine: Full Body apart is the gameplay. The puzzle mechanics are incredibly engaging and challenging, and the game constantly keeps you on your toes with its twists and turns. The added content in the Full Body version only adds to the overall experience, with new levels and storylines that keep you invested in the game even after hours of playtime.Of course, a game like this wouldn't be complete without a captivating storyline, and Catherine: Full Body delivers in spades. The game tackles mature themes like love, lust, and infidelity, and explores the psychology behind these complex emotions in a way that is both entertaining and thought-provoking.My only minor gripe with the game is that some of the puzzle levels can feel repetitive after a while, but the overall experience is so enjoyable that it hardly detracts from the game's overall quality.In short, Catherine: Full Body is a must-play for anyone who loves puzzle games, thrilling narratives, and unforgettable characters. It's a mind-bending thrill ride that will keep you hooked from start to finish. Highly recommended! Read more 3 people found this helpful Helpful Report Thomas & Jessii4.0 out of 5 stars Mediocre, and predictable story, but outstanding gameplay Reviewed in the United States on March 11, 2020Verified Purchase The story here is fairly straightforward, with some fun twists, but it never got very interesting. The "nightmare" puzzles however are absolutely fun. It's essentially a twist on QBert with a lot of added traps and elements that build over the course of the game. The difficulty can get very high, and replaying at higher levels of difficulty is a great challenge. Even the "Rapunzel" mini-game which is a simplified block puzzle game inside the main story is a lot of fun and has a lot of levels to channel you.The game has a lot of style and is very adult oriented as you can tell. This is not a game for anyone under 14. The story itself is both violent and risque, but even by current broadcast media standards, is also pretty tame. There is no full nudity in the game, also surprising given the framing of the remaster of the game for PS4.It's an odd game with that is both very strange, a lot of fun, and a big challenge for those who want to go full out with the puzzles. Definitely worth a play! Read more 10 people found this helpful Helpful Report Jacob5.0 out of 5 stars Fresh update to an old game.
